description: Roseau Load Flow is a distribution-network load-flow and static-analysis package developed by Roseau Technologies. Its Python interface uses unit-aware quantities and a C++ solver for unbalanced multiphase networks. Documented features include explicit neutral and grounding connections, flexible loads with Volt-Watt and Volt-VAr controls, centre-tapped transformers and single-wire earth-return arrangements. The package includes 20 low-voltage and 20 medium-voltage feeder examples with summer and winter load points. Simulation geography and network resolution are user-defined; these examples are not a universal distribution inventory. Public Python source is available under BSD-3-Clause, while the solver has separate licence terms. The README offers free solver use up to 50 buses and free licences on request for students and teachers; larger personal or commercial use requires contacting the provider. The complete product is therefore recorded as freemium, although its open-source portion is free. Python 3.12 or newer is required. Outputs include load-flow results and network or voltage-profile plots. It supports distribution capacity and operating studies and is comparable in purpose to pandapower (model-pandapower), without implying tested interchangeability.
